title: StochasticSmoothAndConvex.lean

problem_class.label: convex
problem_class.details: Unconstrained minimization of a differentiable convex function f:E→ℝ with globally L-Lipschitz gradient. A global minimizer xstar exists with ‖x0−xstar‖≤R. Parameters satisfy L>0, R≥0, σ≥0, and ε>0; strong convexity is not required.

oracle.label: stochastic_gradient
oracle.details: Each query x returns G(x,ω)∈E, with E[G(x,ω)]=∇f(x) and E[‖G(x,ω)−∇f(x)‖²]≤σ². The oracle is jointly measurable and has the stated first- and second-moment integrability. Fresh seeds are independent and identically distributed across calls. Only gradient vectors are returned; objective values are unavailable.
oracle.evidence: LongTails/Setups/StochasticSmoothAndConvex.lean: IsStochasticGradient.measurable, integrable, unbiased, variance_integrable, variance; spec.admissible oracle law and answer.

distinctive_assumptions.label: bounded_variance
distinctive_assumptions.details: Uniform centered second-moment bound E[‖G(x,ω)−∇f(x)‖²]≤σ² for every x. No almost-sure noise bound or exponential-tail assumption is imposed; σ=0 is permitted.

distinctive_assumptions.label: other
distinctive_assumptions.details: E is a real complete, second-countable Hilbert space with its Borel measurable structure; finite dimensionality is not required. All Params, including L, R, σ, ε, and x0, are public. The objective, seed distribution, and oracle map are hidden. Oracle seeds have an infinite product law, giving independent samples across calls.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/StochasticSmoothAndConvex.lean: Params; spec.Public, publicInput, Instance, and admissible.

accuracy.label: objective_gap
accuracy.details: The output is an E-valued measurable random point. For a global minimizer xstar, f(output)−f(xstar) must be integrable and have expectation at most ε. No particular iterate or averaging rule is prescribed.

accuracy.label: expected
accuracy.details: The objective-gap guarantee is in expectation over the product of algorithm randomness and oracle randomness. Each supplied budget bounds the number of oracle calls for every seed realization; it is a fixed budget rather than an expected-cost bound.

setup_category.label: classical
setup_category.reason: This is the standard smooth convex stochastic first-order optimization formulation with independent unbiased gradients, uniformly bounded variance, a known initial-distance bound, and expected objective-gap accuracy, stated in a separable Hilbert space.

descriptionHtml:
Stochastic Smooth Convex Minimization

We consider minimizing a differentiable convex function f:E→R on a separable real Hilbert space E. Its gradient is L-Lipschitz, where L>0, and a given point x0∈E lies within distance R≥0 of a global minimizer x⋆. At x, the oracle returns an unbiased stochastic gradient with variance at most σ2, where σ≥0, using independent samples across calls. For ε>0, the goal is a measurable output x¯∈E with integrable objective gap satisfying E[f(x¯)−f(x⋆)]≤ε, where expectation includes both algorithm and oracle randomness.

The optimization problem is minx∈Ef(x). The norm ∥⋅∥ is induced by the inner product on E. Let Ω be the measurable sample space. The algorithm receives E, Ω, L, R, σ, ε, and x0; the objective and sampling distribution are accessed through the oracle.

Our assumptions:

Assumption 1 (Convexity). For every x,y∈E and t∈[0,1], f((1−t)x+ty)≤(1−t)f(x)+tf(y).

Assumption 2 (Smoothness). The function f is Fréchet differentiable everywhere on E, and its gradient satisfies ∥∇f(x)−∇f(y)∥≤L∥x−y∥,x,y∈E.

Assumption 3 (Initial distance). There exists x⋆∈E such that f(x⋆)≤f(x)for every x∈E,∥x0−x⋆∥≤R.

Assumption 4 (Stochastic gradients). There exist a probability measure p on Ω and a jointly measurable map g:E×Ω→E. For every x∈E, the map g(x,⋅) is Bochner integrable under p, the squared error ∥g(x,⋅)−∇f(x)∥2 is integrable under p, and Eξ∼p[g(x,ξ)]=∇f(x),Eξ∼p[∥g(x,ξ)−∇f(x)∥2]≤σ2. At call k, a query xk∈E receives g(xk,ξk), where (ξk)k≥0 are independent with common law p and are independent of the algorithm’s randomness.

Queries may be made at any point of E and may depend on previous replies. After the allotted oracle calls, the output x¯ must be measurable and its objective gap must be integrable, with EP[f(x¯)−f(x⋆)]≤ε, where P is the joint law of the algorithm’s randomness and the oracle samples.

Efficient Methods for Stochastic Composite Optimization. 2008 (21 June author preprint; journal version titled An optimal method for stochastic composite optimization, 2012, online 2011). Complexity: O(1+LR2/ε+σ2R2/ε2) stochastic-gradient oracle calls, fixed cost, for expected objective gap at most ε; AC-SA specialized to a Euclidean ball of radius R containing a minimizer.
  • Andrei Kulunchakov and Julien Mairal. Estimate Sequences for Stochastic Composite Optimization: Variance Reduction, Acceleration, and Robustness to Noise. 2020. Complexity: O(1+LR2/ε+σ2R2/ε2) stochastic-gradient oracle calls, fixed cost including one initialization call, for expected objective gap at most ε; proximal accelerated SGD.

comparisonHtml:
Convex differentiable f:E→R on a second-countable real Hilbert space with its Borel σ-algebra; ∇f is L-Lipschitz and a global minimizer x⋆ satisfies ∥x0−x⋆∥≤R. Here L,ε>0 and R,σ≥0. The jointly measurable oracle g has integrable values and squared errors, with ∫g(x,ω)dp(ω)=∇f(x) and ∫∥g(x,ω)−∇f(x)∥2dp(ω)≤σ2 for a probability law p. Samples are IID, P=p⊗N. The target is measurable output x^ with integrable gap and ∫[f(x^)−f(x⋆)]dP≤ε. The setup imposes no algorithm restriction.

Stochastic smooth convex minimization: StochasticSmoothAndConvex.
Result Oracle complexity Novelty Limitations
(1) AcceleratedStochasticConvex (Ours) (review) O(1+LR2ε+σ2R2ε2)
(2) SgdConvex (Ours) (review) O(1+LR2ε+σ2R2ε2)
(3) AC-SA (Ghadimi and Lan 2012), Prop. 7, (4.10)–(4.11). Unconstrained Euclidean specialization. O(1+LR2ε+σ2R2ε2) (1): Matches known rate; Lean formalization in Hilbert space of a dimension-free analysis. (2): Matches when σ2≥Lε. (2): At σ=0, LR2/ε≥1, costs O(LR2/ε) versus O(LR2/ε).
(4) Smooth SGD (Bubeck 2015), Thm. 6.3 proof. Derived bound: unconstrained Euclidean quadratic mirror map. O(1+LR2ε+σ2R2ε2) (2): Matches known rate; Lean formalization. Step omits R, but stopping still needs it; no reduction in required information.
(5) AC-SA (Ghadimi and Lan 2012), Prop. 7, (4.5), (4.10)–(4.12). Bounded convex X⊂Rd. O(1+LR2ε+σ2(R2+DX2)ℓ2ε2) stochastic gradients and projections onto X; Pr{f(x^)−minXf≤ε}≥1−δ. Requires DX<∞, σ>0, and ∫exp⁡(∥g−∇f∥2/σ2)dp≤e at every x∈X. (1), (2): No established improvement for this probability target. Different domain and accuracy guarantees prevent direct rate comparison. (1), (2): Expectation only; no corresponding high-probability guarantee.

Abbr: Costs count individual stochastic-gradient calls; in (5) each call also uses one projection. R bounds initial distance to the relevant minimizer; σ2 is the variance bound; ε is objective-gap accuracy. In (5), DX=supx∈X∥x−x⋆∥, δ∈(0,1), ℓ=1+log⁡(1/δ). Euclidean specializations use V(u,v)=∥u−v∥2/2 and zero composite term; (4) uses initial Bregman distance rather than domain diameter.

import LongTails.Template
import Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.Gradient.Basic
import Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Function.L2Space
import Mathlib.Probability.ProductMeasure
import Mathlib.Analysis.Convex.Function

open MeasureTheory

namespace LongTails.Setups.StochasticSmoothAndConvex

open OracleTemplate

section

variable (E : Type*) (Ω : Type) [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E]
    [CompleteSpace E] [MeasurableSpace E] [MeasurableSpace Ω]

structure IsStochasticGradient (p : Measure Ω) [IsProbabilityMeasure p]
    (f : E → ℝ) (oracle : E → Ω → E) (σ : ℝ) : Prop where
  measurable : Measurable (Function.uncurry oracle)
  integrable : ∀ x, Integrable (oracle x) p
  unbiased : ∀ x, ∫ ω, oracle x ω ∂p = gradient f x
  variance_integrable : ∀ x, Integrable (fun ω => ‖oracle x ω-gradient f x‖^2) p
  variance : ∀ x, ∫ ω, ‖oracle x ω-gradient f x‖^2 ∂p ≤ σ^2

end

structure Params where
  E : Type u
  [normedE : NormedAddCommGroup E]
  [linearE : InnerProductSpace ℝ E]
  [completeE : CompleteSpace E]
  [measurableE : MeasurableSpace E]
  [borelE : BorelSpace E]
  [countableE : SecondCountableTopology E]
  Ω : Type
  [measurableΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω]
  L : ℝ
  R : ℝ
  σ : ℝ
  ε : ℝ
  x0 : E

attribute [instance] Params.normedE Params.linearE Params.completeE Params.measurableE Params.borelE Params.countableE Params.measurableΩ

abbrev spec : Setup where
  Params := Params
  Public := Params
  Instance p := p.E → ℝ
  Query p := p.E
  Reply p := p.E
  Output p := p.E
  publicInput p := p
  valid q := 0 < q.L ∧ 0 ≤ q.R ∧ 0 ≤ q.σ ∧ 0 < q.ε
  admissible q f O :=
    ∃ (oracle : q.E → q.Ω → q.E) (p : ProbabilityMeasure q.Ω),
    O = { Seed := fun _ => q.Ω
          law := ⟨Measure.infinitePi (fun _ : ℕ => (p : Measure q.Ω)), inferInstance⟩
          answer := fun _ (_, x) seed => oracle x seed } ∧
    ConvexOn ℝ Set.univ f ∧
    (∀ x, HasGradientAt f (gradient f x) x) ∧
    (∀ x y, ‖gradient f x - gradient f y‖ ≤ q.L * ‖x - y‖) ∧
    (∃ xstar, IsMinOn f Set.univ xstar ∧ ‖q.x0 - xstar‖ ≤ q.R) ∧
    IsStochasticGradient q.E q.Ω p f oracle q.σ
  successful q f output P :=
    Measurable output ∧
    ∃ xstar, IsMinOn f Set.univ xstar ∧
      Integrable (fun ω => f (output ω) - f xstar) (P : Measure _) ∧
      (∫ ω, f (output ω) - f xstar ∂(P : Measure _)) ≤ q.ε

end LongTails.Setups.StochasticSmoothAndConvex
